chunks: From the slave of Allah, 'Ali, Commander of the Faithful,

to the people who became wrathful for the sake of Allah when He was disobeyed on His earth and His rights were ignored, and oppression had spread its coverings over the virtuous as well as the vicious, on the local as well as the foreigner. Consequently, no good was acted upon nor any evil was avoided.

key_terms.سُرَادِقَهُ: Its coverings/tents (metaphor for the spread of oppression)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Ali say about the nature of oppression in his letter to the Egyptians?
ai.summary: This letter, part of the administrative correspondence in *Nahj al-Balagha*, reflects Imam Ali’s response to the Egyptian populace's anger over the Umayyad usurpation of the Caliphate, framing their grievance as a divine cause (*ghadab li-llah*). The description of justice (*adl*) being overshadowed by tyranny (*jawr*) underscores the Shia concept of political legitimacy tied to moral rectitude, where the breakdown of social order affects both the righteous and the wicked alike. It serves as a foundational text for understanding the socio-political climate of the early Islamic period and the Imam’s emphasis on restoring divine law through just governance.
